newsitem.title: CANADA: Toronto stocks end sharply lower on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: Toronto stocks end sharply lower on profit taking.

text.p: Toronto stocks ended sharply lower on Wednesday as investors continued to grab profits on Canada's biggest stock market.
The TSE 300 Composite Index sank 48.25 points to close at 6257.21, extending Tuesday's decline.
The key index hit a lifetime high of 6348.02 on Tuesday before profit takers stepped in to push the market lower.
"I think you have to put a lot of this down to good old profit taking," said Fred Ketchen, director of equity trading for ScotiaMcLeod Inc.
In today's action, trading was brisk with turnover of 100 million shares worth C$1.6 billion ($1.17 billion).
The financial services group lost 80 points as bank stocks extended their recent correction. High-flying banks have pushed the TSE to record highs in the past several months.
Toronto's 12 weak sectors also included gold and precious metals, transportation, conglomerates and industrial products.
Canadian high-tech stocks were depressed on Wednesday by a selloff in U.S. technology shares which pulled Nasdaq lower.
Toronto's two strong sectors were forestry products and consumer products.
Ketchen said concern over the timing of a possible U.S. interest rate hike also weighed on stock markets today. But he predicted Toronto has not seen its peak for 1997.
"I don't think we've seen the highs for the year at all. I think there is a lot of good stuff still ahead," he said.
* Among Canada's big banks, Royal Bank of Canada fell 1.25 to 59.40 on 1.0 million shares. Bank of Montreal dropped 0.50 to finish at 53.75 on 966,000 shares.
* Bombardier Inc. class B surrendered 0.45 to 26.15 despite reporting record fourth-quarter profits. Analysts said the earnings came in on target.
* BioChem Pharma Inc. jumped 1.10 to 78.60 after the biotechnology firm reported higher fourth quarter profits. BioChem also announced plans for a 2-for-1 stock split.
